expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: Defines `export type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription;` with each type having `status: 'trialing'`, `status: 'active'`, etc.

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: TrialingSubscription has only trialEndDate, ActiveSubscription has only renewalDate, PastDueSubscription has retryCount/gracePeriodEnd, CanceledSubscription has cancelReason/isVoluntary. No field bleeding between types.

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Shows `default: const _exhaustiveCheck: never = sub; return _exhaustiveCheck;` in the switch statement

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Uses `id: string; userId: string; planId: string;` — all bare strings, not branded types

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: No transition function or constraint mechanism provided; only type definitions shown

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Mentions preventing one mistake in passing ('preventing you from accidentally accessing a field like `trialEndDate` on an `active` subscription') but does not systematically enumerate which misuses are prevented

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Recommends discriminated unions throughout; no optional-field pattern presented
